page: Microsoft Azure HB368-288rs_v5 is a compute-focused virtual machine belonging to the High Performance Computing family, configured under Microsoft Hyper-V. Built on an x86_64 Intel processor architecture, the instance provides 288 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 448.0 GB of system memory. This resource distribution yields approximately 1.56 GB of memory per core, reflecting an architecture optimized for dense parallel processing rather than memory-heavy footprints. The instance does not feature discrete GPUs, concentrating system capability entirely on central processing tasks.

Storage and network configurations are structured for high-throughput operational demands. The server integrates 15,874 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, providing substantial low-latency local capacity for temporary files and high-rate disk transactions. Additionally, the instance is RDMA capable and supports Premium Storage configurations, facilitating low-latency node-to-node communication across cluster topologies. Public IPv4 networking is not provisioned as a complimentary allocation with this server type.

From a cost and resource perspective, high compute core density coupled with large-scale local NVMe capacity offers strong efficiency for tasks that require massive parallel execution without requiring large per-core memory allocations. The primary tradeoff lies in the comparatively constrained 1.56 GB per-core RAM ratio, which limits suitability for memory-intensive in-memory data structures. Microsoft Azure HB368-288rs_v5 is appropriate for distributed High Performance Computing tasks, computational fluid dynamics, finite element analysis, molecular dynamics, and IOPS-heavy temporary scratch processing.
